name: HeyGen
tagline: Video avatars for training and sales video
description: Generates video with a human avatar, translation and automatic dubbing in dozens of languages, useful for training, content and sales video at scale.
priceNote: Pricing as of October 2026; plans change — check the official site.
bestFor: Training video and content in several languages without filming
pros: Avatar with natural expression and gestures, which lands well in internal training video
Translation and automatic dubbing deliver the same video in dozens of languages
Produces the video in minutes, which lets you publish daily content without a production team
API available to build video generation into a support or onboarding flow
cons: Credit billing, 20 to 48 per minute depending on the avatar, gets expensive fast on a series for social media
In close-up the avatar betrays that it is artificial and mishandles hands and pronunciation
Control of gestures and framing is limited, so you cannot produce cinema-grade work
For high-ticket sales video, a real presenter still converts better

features.name: Realistic avatars
features.detail: Library of presenters with natural expressions and gestures

features.name: Text to video
features.detail: Write the script and generate the video with an avatar narrating

features.name: Translation and dubbing
features.detail: Translates the video and replicates the voice with lip sync

features.name: Voice clone
features.detail: Builds a voice from a sample so the brand presenter can speak

features.name: Templates and API
features.detail: Ready templates per format and an API to generate video inside a flow

useCases: Sales training module with the same script in English and Spanish
Welcome video for a new customer, with the company name and the proposal
Daily content for social media where only the script text changes
Product tutorial sent inside the platform, with no screen or voice recording
bestForWho: Companies with a sales or training team spread across several countries that need video at scale.
verdict: HeyGen solves a very specific and very useful case: keeping the same training content in several languages without hiring a localization team, and the dubbing with lip sync is the highlight. Where the tool still does not replace a real presenter is sales video, because audiences notice the avatar in close-up and conversion drops. Cost deserves attention too: billing is per credit, and two minutes of video per week across several languages overruns the entry plan quota within a few months. For a small company, use it at most for internal training and short videos, and the Creator plan covers that well. For a larger company, the Business plan with the API pays off when video production becomes part of other tools' flows and needs automation.
